summary: Why your organisation exists. The vision says where it wants to get to, and the mission says what it does to get there.
example: Vision: every member family earns a fair living from what it grows. Mission: we collect, check and sell our members' produce together.
definition: The purpose is why everything in the strategy exists, stated once at its top: the vision, a future state of the world the organisation serves, and the mission, what the organisation does and for whom to get there. It is not an aim: goals say what the organisation sets out to do, and each is judged Relevant against this. Quote a published plan's words verbatim, with the plan and section as the source.

/spec/vision.guide: The future the organisation is working towards, in one or two sentences: the state of the world it wants, not what it does. No figures: those belong to the goals' measures.
good: Every member can make a dependable living from what they grow.

poor.why: A target, not a vision: the figure and the date belong in a key result under a goal.
Says nothing a goal could be judged against: best at what, for whom?

poor.text: We collect, check and sell our members' produce.
poor.why: What the organisation does is the mission; the vision is the future it is working towards.

/spec/mission.guide: What the organisation does to get there, and for whom, in one or two sentences. It names the standing work, not a list of projects.
good: We collect, check and sell our members' produce together, so each member gets a fair and dependable price for a season's work.

poor.text: Roll out quality checks at every depot and open two new depots.
poor.why: A list of pieces of work that end, which are projects; the mission is what the organisation does all the time.
Values, not a mission: they do not say what the organisation does.

/spec/source.guide: Where the vision and mission are published, precisely enough to find again: the document, and the section or page. Leave it empty when they are written here first.

poor.why: Not precise enough to find again, and a page that changes is not a source.

/metadata/name.guide: What to call it on screen, such as Purpose, or the plan's own word for its vision and mission.
